content: GOAL: orient before ideating (round 20261028_233100_128, ideation_4). READ: tool catalog + prompt. OBSERVED: append_progress available at tools.progress.append_progress; no write/shell. REASONING: will inspect repo for existing SID/hyperbolic mechanisms to avoid copying, then emit one idea. OPEN: what code exists locally.

STAGE: design-space audit before writing the idea.
GOAL: find a coupling position not already occupied by rounds 1258/2120/2212 or their fork-* family.
READ: prompt + the earlier-round census (fork-angle-transport, fork-angular-barycenter, fork-radial-volume, fork_shell_transport, successor-cone-contrast, BRANCHCURV-SID, GEO-SHELL-RQ, GEOPFX-SID, GEO_REPAIR, GYRO-TARGET-RQ, KAPPA_BRANCH, LORENTZ_CONE_RQ, SUCC-TAN-RQ, behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts, cocond-markov-poincare-ot, CURVCELL-SID, SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ). No repo read access (permission denied) so the census is the only overlap evidence.
OBSERVED: every listed mechanism is either (a) a weighting/diffusion of assignment mass, (b) a purely negative-curvature hierarchy (radial shell / branch fan / curvature field), (c) tangent-space transport or angular barycentre of successors, or (d) Lorentz cone. Nothing listed uses a SPHERICAL (positive-curvature) factor, nothing uses a mixed-curvature product metric, and nothing makes a per-item behaviour statistic select which curvature the quantizer measures that item under.
REASONING: a single-curvature hyperbolic SID assumes the transition graph is tree-like. Real sequential behaviour is a mixture: sequel/attribute chains are tree-like, but repeat consumption, substitutes and mutually-linked co-consumption are cyclic, and a ball cannot place cycles cheaply (it must spend radial depth to close a loop). A product of a Poincare factor and a spherical factor, with a per-item measured tree-likeness g_i gating the two factors inside the assignment metric and inside the codebook Frechet mean, is a materially different coupling position: behaviour sets which geometry the item is quantized under, geometry sets the token partition.
OPEN: write the single proposal (MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ) with equations, safeguards, cost at 24556 items / 24 steps / 3000 epochs.

STAGE: final answer (single idea).
GOAL: deliver one in-scope proposal in the required block format.
OBSERVED: proposal = MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, a behaviour-gated mixed-curvature product codebook. Behaviour signal = per-item directed local clustering coefficient C_i of the Stage-2 training transition graph, giving tree-likeness g_i = clip(1 - C_i, 0.1, 0.9), 0.5 if out-degree < 5. Geometry = trainable product of a Poincare ball (k_H init -1, arcosh distance, exp0/log0) and a sphere (k_S init +1, arccos geodesic, radius 1/sqrt(k_S)), each factor distance normalised by its own derived maximum.
COUPLING: the same g_i multiplies the squared normalised hyperbolic distance and (1-g_i) the spherical one inside the per-level RQ assignment, and the same g_i weights the Karcher/Frechet update of every product codebook entry. Behaviour therefore selects the metric an item is quantized under, geometry places the codes it is measured against; removing either changes the assignment and the codebook estimator (behaviour-off: g_i = 0.5 everywhere; geometry-off: k_H,k_S -> 0, i.e. plain behaviour-weighted Euclidean RQ).
WHY DISTINCT: the earlier census (fork-* transport, BRANCHCURV, GEO-SHELL, KAPPA_BRANCH, CURVCELL, LORENTZ_CONE, GYRO-TARGET, SUCC-TAN, behaviour-anchored charts, cocond-markov-poincare-ot) is entirely assignment-mass weighting, single negative-curvature hierarchy, tangent transport, or a Lorentz cone. None uses positive curvature, a product manifold, or a per-item behaviour statistic as a curvature-mixing coordinate.
CONSTRAINTS: no tuning (clip bounds fixed defaults, curvatures trainable from unit init, normalisers derived from current curvature, baseline temperature and lr reused); no ablation arm trained (three switches exist as flags, only both-on runs once); cost ~7.9e5 product distances per step over 3 levels at 1023 items/step, well under 1 percent of a Stage-2 step, plus a one-time O(E) graph pass.
OPEN: nothing for this round; the single frozen-budget run decides it against Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.065.
